savings.title: Money style
savings.question: What's your money style right now?

options.title: Enjoy life
options.blurb: More fun now. Less of what's left goes to the future.

options.title: Balanced
options.blurb: Some for fun, a good chunk for later.

options.title: Save hard
options.blurb: Almost everything left after bills goes to the future.

invest.title: Where the money goes
invest.question: Where should your new savings go?

options.title: Play it safe
options.blurb: Mostly provident funds and deposits. Steady and boring.

options.title: A bit of everything
options.blurb: Shares for growth, provident funds and gold for cushion.

options.title: Go for growth
options.blurb: Mostly shares. Bigger swings, bigger upside over decades.

marry.title: Marriage
marry.question: Is marriage on the cards in the next few years?

options.title: Not yet
options.blurb: Career and savings first. You can decide again later.

options.title: Around 27
options.blurb: An early start to family life.

options.title: Around 30
options.blurb: A bit later and a bit more settled.

marryLater.title: Marriage
marryLater.question: Is marriage on the cards in the next few years?

options.title: Not planning to
options.blurb: Stay single, at least for this stretch of life.

options.title: Around 34
options.blurb: Later, with a career already built.

options.title: Around 38
options.blurb: Much later. Fewer family years to plan for.

options.title: Small and simple
options.blurb: Family and close friends. About ₹5 lakh in today's money.

options.title: A proper celebration
options.blurb: Both families, a good venue. About ₹15 lakh in today's money.

options.title: The big fat wedding
options.blurb: Hundreds of guests, several days. About ₹40 lakh in today's money.

options.title: Looks after the home
options.blurb: One income. Everyday costs are shared by two.

options.title: Works part-time
options.blurb: Earns about a third of what you do, after their own tax.

options.title: Works full-time
options.blurb: Earns about four-fifths of what you do, after their own tax.

options.title: No children
options.blurb: More room in the budget, a quieter home.

options.title: One child
options.blurb: About ₹30 to 50 lakh in today's money by age 21, and school and college fees rise faster than prices.

options.title: Two children
options.blurb: Double the cost, three years apart. Fees keep outrunning prices.

home.title: A home of your own
home.question: Keep renting, or buy a home?

options.title: Keep renting
options.blurb: Light on cash and easy to move. Rent rises with prices and you own nothing at the end.

options.title: Buy a home
options.blurb: A 20-year loan for most of the price, an instalment that never pauses, and a home that tends to grow in value.

emergency.title: Emergency fund
emergency.question: How much cash will you keep for a rainy day?

options.title: Wing it
options.blurb: No separate cushion. Every spare rupee gets invested.

options.title: 3 months
options.blurb: Three months of bills sit in cash before you invest.

options.title: 6 months
options.blurb: Six months of bills in cash. Safe, but cash earns very little.

health.title: Health insurance
health.question: Will you buy your own health cover?

options.title: Rely on work's cover
options.blurb: Your employer's small cover is free, but it ends if you lose the job.

options.title: Basic cover
options.blurb: ₹5 lakh of cover. About ₹12,000 a year at 30, rising with age.

options.title: Strong cover
options.blurb: ₹25 lakh of cover. About ₹30,000 a year at 30, rising with age.

growth.title: Invest in yourself
growth.question: How much will you invest in getting better at what you do?

options.title: Coast
options.blurb: Do the job well. No extra courses or effort.

options.title: Keep learning
options.blurb: Some courses and mentors, a few evenings a week. About 2% of your pay.

options.title: Go all in
options.blurb: Certifications, side projects, long evenings. About 6% of your pay, and real risk of burnout.

retirementStyle.title: Life after work
retirementStyle.question: How will you live once you stop working?

options.title: Comfortable
options.blurb: Keep living just as you do now: all of your everyday costs carry on.

options.title: Modest
options.blurb: Cut back a little: about three-quarters of your everyday costs.

options.title: Lean
options.blurb: Live carefully on a little over half of your everyday costs.

retire.title: Retirement age
retire.question: When do you want to stop working?

options.title: At 55
options.blurb: Early exit. Fewer years to earn, more to fund.

options.title: At 60
options.blurb: The classic.

options.title: At 65
options.blurb: Keep going. More earning years, a shorter retirement.

provenance.basis: Illustrative game tuning: savings shares, learning cost as a share of pay, and how much effort each learning level takes (see capability.json for what skills do to pay and how they fade). Not drawn from data. The three-track capability model is for v2. The three savings mixes are game presets; new savings follow the mix, existing holdings are never sold to rebalance. Insurance covers and premiums, and the emergency-fund sizes, are illustrative round numbers. The home decision is offered only while the player rents; whether they can afford it is worked out from their cash and savings (see housing.json). Marriage, wedding size, the partner's work and children are asked only when they apply (see onlyIf in engine/stages.js). Wedding sizes are game presets of 5, 15 and 40 lakh in today's rupees; see family.json for the household and child cost assumptions. Retirement spending levels (100%, 75% and 55% of the last working year's everyday costs) are game presets; see retirement.json for pensions, how long life lasts and what changes at retirement.
